title: Upper Gastrointestinal Bleed
scenario: A 54-year-old male presents to the emergency department after vomiting bright red blood twice at home and passing several black, tarry stools over the past day. He appears pale and diaphoretic.

lines: 54-year-old male brought in by wife after two episodes of hematemesis (bright red) at home and multiple melena stools over 24 hours. Reports history of daily NSAID use for chronic back pain and heavy alcohol intake. Skin pale, cool, and diaphoretic. Alert but anxious and lightheaded. Denies chest pain.
Two large-bore IV lines placed. Type and crossmatch, CBC, and coagulation studies drawn. NPO. Cardiac monitor and continuous SpO2 applied. Provider notified.
Normal saline bolus infusing. IV pantoprazole administered per order. One unit packed red blood cells started per order after consent obtained. NG tube inserted, returned coffee-ground drainage.
Post-transfusion and endoscopy with band ligation completed. Client reports feeling less dizzy. Skin warmer, color improved. No further emesis; NG output cleared.
Ibuprofen 800 mg PO three times daily (home use)
Pantoprazole 80 mg IV bolus, then 8 mg/hr infusion
Octreotide 50 mcg IV bolus, then infusion
Infuse 1 L normal saline bolus, reassess
Type and crossmatch; transfuse 1 unit PRBC
Insert nasogastric tube to low intermittent suction
Notify provider for SBP < 90 or HR > 120

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.rationale: Active hematemesis, hypotension, tachycardia, and pallor with diaphoresis signal significant blood loss and hypovolemia requiring urgent intervention.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each finding, click to specify whether it indicates active bleeding, hypovolemia, or both. Each finding may support more than one.
children.rationale: Melena and elevated BUN reflect digested blood in the GI tract, while low BP and tachycardia reflect hypovolemia. A low hemoglobin results from both ongoing loss and depleted volume.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse determines that the priority problem is {1}, and the most immediate goal is {2}.
children.rationale: Ongoing blood loss with hypotension and tachycardia makes decreased cardiac output from hypovolemia the priority; restoring circulating volume with fluids and blood is the most immediate goal.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client.
children.rationale: Large-bore access, NPO status, and a PPI support resuscitation and reduce rebleeding. Oral iron and continued NSAIDs are inappropriate during active upper GI bleeding.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: When administering the packed red blood cell transfusion, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Verify the blood product with a second nurse
Obtain a baseline set of vital signs before starting
Stay with the client for the first 15 minutes
Infuse the unit with dextrose 5% in water
Warm the unit in a microwave before hanging

children.rationale: Two-nurse verification, baseline vitals, and close monitoring during the first 15 minutes catch transfusion reactions early. Blood is infused only with normal saline and never heated in a microwave.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which findings indicate the treatment has been effective? Select all that apply.

options.text: NG drainage cleared with no further emesis

children.rationale: A normalizing blood pressure and heart rate, warm well-perfused skin, and resolution of bleeding show hemodynamic stability is restored. Persistent pallor and diaphoresis would indicate ongoing instability.
